title: The Unit Circle and Exact Values

sections.heading: Section 1: Coordinates on the Unit Circle

questions.q: On the unit circle, what do the coordinates $(x, y)$ of a point at angle $\theta$ represent?
questions.answer: By definition of the unit circle ($r = 1$), the horizontal coordinate is $x = \cos\theta$ and the vertical coordinate is $y = \sin\theta$.

questions.q: Find the exact coordinates on the unit circle corresponding to $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.
Find the exact coordinates on the unit circle for $\theta = \frac{4\pi}{3}$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Reference Angles and Signs by Quadrant

questions.answer: $\tan\theta = y/x$. It is positive where $x$ and $y$ have the same sign: Quadrant I (both positive) and Quadrant III (both negative).

questions.q: If $\cos\theta < 0$ and $\sin\theta > 0$, in which quadrant does the terminal ray of $\theta$ lie?

sections.heading: Section 3: Exact Values of the Six Trig Functions

questions.answer: Reference angle is $\pi/3$. In Quadrant II, tangent is negative: $-\tan(\pi/3) = -\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Quadrantal Angles and Negative Angles

questions.q: Which of the following values is undefined?

questions.answer: Cosine is an even function: $\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta$. Thus $\cos(-\pi/3) = \cos(\pi/3) = 1/2$.
Sine is an odd function: $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta$. Thus $\sin(-\pi/4) = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
